summary: The appellants, former tenants in 'Madhav Baug', Andheri, were promised alternate accommodation under a 2013 redevelopment agreement and a 2015 Indemnity-cum-Undertaking, which stipulated allotment of two flats (301 and 302) if approvals were not obtained within six months. When redevelopment stalled, the NCDRC dismissed the complaint as time-barred, calculating limitation from July 2015. The Supreme Court held that a continuing cause of action existed due to ongoing negotiations and escrow arrangements. The complaint, filed in February 2019, sought registration of already-received flats and protection from third-party alienation, not initial allotment. The Court ruled that limitation did not bar the claim as the cause of action was fresh upon escrow’s release of the flats in December 2018.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 67 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Section 24-A of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986
final_judgment: The appeal is allowed. The impugned order of the NCDRC dismissing the complaint on limitation grounds is set aside. The complaint is remanded to the NCDRC for decision on merits. The appellants are entitled to costs.
